configuration.enablement: Selected by default. `STY` selects this rule and `STY001` selects only it. `lint.ignore = ["STY001"]`, a matching `lint.per-file-ignores` entry, or removing `builtin` from `plugins` removes the rule from the enabled set before it runs. A `stilyagi: disable STY001` directive instead suppresses reported findings after evaluation; the rule still evaluates over the document.

examples.title: A line break ends the run

rule.explanation: Two or more identical alphabetic tokens separated only by spaces or tabs are reported as a repeated run. Comparison is exact, so `the the` is a run and `The the` is not. A run never crosses markup, a region boundary, a line break, or a synthetic region, and inline code is excluded. The `TOKENS` capability is supplied by the builtin pack's in-process tokenizer; no NLP model or external provider is loaded.
rule.fixes: The rule may propose an unsafe edit that removes the repeated suffix. Apply it only with `stilyagi check --fix --unsafe-fixes`; `--fix` alone skips it, and the `lint.fixable` policy still decides whether the code may contribute an edit. Review the diff before applying it, because a deliberate repetition such as `had had` is removed just as an accidental one is.
limitations: Matching is exact and adjacent: `the the` is a run, but `the plan the plan` is not because other words intervene.
A deliberate repetition is reported the same way as an accidental one, and the unsafe edit cannot tell them apart.
Only headings, paragraphs, and table cells are inspected; inline code, code blocks, and unsupported regions are not.
Synthetic segment text that cannot be mapped to source bytes is not editable, so no edit is offered for it.
Configuration, per-file ignores, and suppression directives can stop a finding; static metadata does not describe effective enablement for a particular file.
rule.name: repeated-word
rule.summary: Report an immediately repeated word in prose.
